changelog: A FULL DESKTOP PASS. The game was built and tuned on a phone, and on a 1920x1080 screen it showed: every overlay was a narrow column pinned to the top of the display, using about a quarter of the width, with rows running under the close button and type sized for a handset. Overlays now use the screen — achievements sit two across in uniform rows beneath a plaque that spans them, How to Play and Settings run in two columns, the army roster grids two or three across instead of one tall stack, and everything centres properly instead of hugging the top edge. SETTINGS READS AS A COMMAND PANEL rather than a scrolling list, and the sound dial's needle is the size it was drawn to be again. THE BATTLE HUD IS SCALED UP — the hand roughly doubles, along with the top bar, the selected-unit card, toasts and coach marks. THE MAP VIEW's bars, buttons and legend all scale with the window, the legend grows to fill the column, and the background is sharp instead of a stretched blur. FULLSCREEN is now an option under Settings. PLAY CHANGES: THE ENEMY TURN IS 50% SLOWER — it had been compressed too far in the last build and resolved faster than you could read it; tap anywhere to skip. NO ROUTE can hand out more than three camps: node types were rolled independently with no view of the map, so a path could deal seven in a row — a route with no fighting on it. OVERCLOCK+ no longer buys a discount; it holds at 2 CP and QUADRUPLES actions and move instead of doubling. And a unit that can both move and aim no longer overflows its details panel.
